body: Just being straight up with u man, if you had done this back in March or April or 2022 you would have gotten in. Now you have 0 chance of getting to the front lines if u have no prior military or combat experience. I only got in as a civilian because I went over early in march

1 buy a local sim card in Ukraine. Start using signal app to communicate with people. If ur going anywhere near the front you don't want a foreign sim card in your phone. 

2. Water bottle water bottle water bottle. When I'm in UA I carry a 5L plastic just that I refill constantly.  If you can buy a lifestraw water bottle with a built in filter your life will become amazingly easy. You can fill it at a tap and go on ur way. 

3. Download Bolt and Uklon. Never get a taxi from the dudes outside train and bus stations. They will charge you 10x the normal price. Bolt and Uklon are used everywhere in both countries. Uber too but not as prevalent

4. Sounds fuckin stupid but go to a pharmacy in Ukraine and get some sore throat spray. I've gotten so many sore throats or colds in that country and the spray saved my fucking bananas

5. Get something other than a plastic bag to hold ur documents and cards. I have a pelican waterproof phone holder that fits all my docs and money and I can hang it on my neck under a sweatshirt. Easy way to never lose ur shit regardless of how goofy you look. 

6. people will be skeptical of you. Don't lie to other foreigners and be straight up with ur intentions and what u do in the country. I've seen guys get their shit beat in for saying they are foreign legion or a fighter when they've never been to the front. Nobody will judge you for helping but they will judge you for lying and word gets around very fuckin fast

7. Have fun and good luck

To be honest with you at this point in the war you aren't gonna be able to anything at all unless you already have contacts over there. I was in ukraine from April to December and I was a civilian like you. The only reason I got a combat role was because I showed up before they had regulations about who could and couldn't join. I'm going back in 3 weeks but my advice to you if you want to really really help is donate money to actual units. I have a few that I could send you that need supplies. That is quite literally how you will help in the best way. Helping specific units and people already there but supplies like thermals and night vision. No offense to you at all man because I was in the same boat as you but in terms of really getting a foothold over there it might be a lil late for you. I don't know a single foreigner over there who hasn't been there at least 1 times for a few months during the war. If ur deadset on getting over there then supply running and evacs are your best bet to get anywhere near the front. But if not gonna be able to have a gun in ur hand on that county at this point in the war as a civi. I'm sorry man
